title: "Advanced" fzf + rg integration - Can the preview grow/shrink dynamically based on the number of results?
body:
<!-- Check all that apply [x] -->

- [x] I have read through the manual page (`man fzf`)
- [x] I have the latest version of fzf
- [x] I have searched through the existing issues

## Info

- OS
    - [x] Linux
    - [x] Mac OS X
    - [ ] Windows
    - [ ] Etc.
- Shell
    - [ ] bash
    - [x] zsh
    - [ ] fish

## Question

I have implemented [the `fzf` + `rg` integration found in `ADVANCED.md`](https://github.com/participant2/fzf/blob/master/ADVANCED.md#ripgrep-integration). It is amazing.

However, it wastes a lot of screen real estate, with the results/preview split fixed at 40%/60%. When almost all the results have been filtered out, this means 40% of the screen is wasted.

Can this "dead space" be dynamically taken up by the preview? For example, by setting the size of the preview window to equal something like `max(60%, 100% - results%)`? So if there are tons of matches, the results would take up 40% and the preview would take up 60%, but if I add to the query such that the number of matches decreases and takes up less than 40%, the preview window will grow to pick up the slack.

Is this currently possible? I know `preview-window` takes a "threshold", however the man page also says "only one alternative layout is allowed", which sounds like dynamic resizing is not possible. But I wanted to confirm.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: In `fzf`, there isn't a pre-existing variable to get the total number of listed items and matched items. However, a workaround exists, although it's somewhat lengthy. This method involves using the `--listen` flag to query `fzf` about the `totalCount` and `matchCount`, and then sending an update to `fzf` to modify the preview size whenever the `matchCount` changes. Writing this as a bash script is should be doable. The image below displays two terminals. The top one shows the standard `fzf` list with a query, while the bottom terminal queries `fzf` in a headless manner[^1]. The maintainer recently provided a related response[^2]. [^1]: [CHANGELOG.md 0.43.0](https://github.com/participant2/fzf/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#0430) [^2]: [Preview window sizing - specify size of finder list instead of preview window · Issue #3570 · participant2/fzf · GitHub ](https://github.com/participant2/fzf/issues/3570#issuecomment-1884109346) --- Alternatively, I often assign a unique keyboard shortcut to change the size of the preview window, allowing me to toggle through the size that suits best. ```bash man fzf … CHANGE PREVIEW WINDOW ATTRIBUTES change-preview-window action can be used to change the properties of the preview window. Unlike the --preview-window option, you can specify mul- tiple sets of options separated by '|' characters. e.g. # Rotate through the options using CTRL-/ fzf --preview 'cat {}' --bind 'ctrl-/:- dow(right,70%|down,40%,border-horizontal|hidden|right)' # The default properties given by `--preview-window` are inherited, so an empty string in the list is interpreted as the default ```

comments.body:
### Prototype for dynamically adjusting the preview window 1. Save the file as `rfv`. 2. Make it executable by running `chmod +x rfv`. 3. Execute it by running `./rfv`. >[!NOTE] > The **minimum** size of the `preview-window` is set inside the `jq` query to `$rows/3`, > and the **maximum** size is `$rows - $buffer_space`.
Script --- ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash set -o allexport -o errexit -o nounset -o pipefail # https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#The-Set-Builtin SHELL=$(which bash) # Set rows to the number of lines in the terminal rows=$(tput lines) buffer_space="5" # =================== helper functions ==================== die() { echo ERROR: "$*" >&2 exit 1 } # Function to send GET/POST request to fzf with optional data load curl_fzf() { command curl --silent --request "$1" --data "${2-}" "localhost:$FZF_PORT" } spin_me() { local old_size="" # Loop as long 'fzf' (parent process) is alive while command kill -0 "$PPID" 2>/dev/null; do # Calculate the new size of the preview window based on the number of matches and rows in # the terminal new_size="$( curl_fzf GET | jq --raw-output --argjson rows "$rows" --argjson buffer_space "$buffer_space" \ '[ ([($rows/3), ($rows - .matchCount - $buffer_space) ] | max), ($rows - $buffer_space) ] | min | floor' )" # If new size is different from old size, update the preview window size and header if [ "$new_size" != "$old_size" ]; then curl_fzf POST "change-header(Preview Window Size: $new_size/ ∑ Rows: $rows)+change-preview-window:$new_size" old_size=$new_size fi sleep 0.5 done } # =================== check requirements ==================== if ((rows <= 1)); then die "'rows' must be higher than 1." fi for tool in curl fzf jq; do if ! type -p $tool >/dev/null; then die "'$tool' was not found." fi done # ===================== let's begin ======================== # https://github.com/participant2/fzf/blob/master/ADVANCED.md#ripgrep-integration rg --color=always --line-number --no-heading --smart-case "${*:-}" | FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS="" fzf \ --ansi \ --bind 'start:execute-silent:spin_me &' \ --color "hl:-1:underline,hl+:-1:underline:reverse" \ --delimiter : \ --listen \ --preview 'bat --color=always {1} --highlight-line {2}' \ --preview-window 'up,border-bottom,+{2}+3/3,~3' \ --bind 'enter:become(vim {1} +{2})' ``` ---

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Thanks so much for that minimal command!

Redirecting to a file helped me find the issue myself: I had set `FZF_API_KEY` elsewhere, but wasn't passing it into the server via `curl`. Hence the requests were being silently rejected and `change-preview-window` was never being triggered.

In the end, the following keybinding works for me and now she's purring like a kitten!

```bash
  --bind=$'change:execute-silent:(
    PREVIEW_SIZE=$(
      curl -qsH "x-api-key: $FZF_API_KEY" localhost:$FZF_PORT \|
        jq -r --argjson LINES $LINES \'[([($LINES/3), ($LINES - .matchCount - 5) ] | max),($LINES - 5)] | min | floor\'
    );
    curl -qsH "x-api-key: $FZF_API_KEY" localhost:$FZF_PORT -d "change-preview-window:$PREVIEW_SIZE"
  ) &'
```

Thanks again for all your help!

I'll close the issue now as it's been resolved. However, @participant1, since I have the individual attention of a board-certified shell+`fzf` wizard like you, I'd like to briefly co-opt this thread with a loosely-related question that's stumped me for weeks.

The following snippet gets sourced from my .zshrc and attempts to configure `fzf`'s `CTRL-T` keybinding in a nice, readable manner:

```bash
export FZF_DEFAULT_COMMAND="fd --color=always --hidden"

FZF_CTRL_T_PREVIEW_COMMAND="bat --color=always --line-range=:500 {}"
FZF_CTRL_T_KEYBINDINGS_ARRAY=(
  "alt-b:become(bat {})"
  "alt-l:become(${${BAT_PAGER}:-less} {})"
  "alt-n:become(${EDITOR:-vim} {})"
)
FZF_CTRL_T_KEYBINDINGS=$(echo "${FZF_CTRL_T_KEYBINDINGS_ARRAY}" | sed 's/) a/),a/g')
FZF_CTRL_T_OPTS_ARRAY=(
  "--bind='${FZF_CTRL_T_KEYBINDINGS}'"
  "--header-first"
  "--no-height"
  "--preview='${FZF_CTRL_T_PREVIEW_COMMAND}'"
  "--preview-window=hidden"
)
FZF_CTRL_T_COMMAND_ARRAY=(
  "${FZF_DEFAULT_COMMAND}"
  "--exclude=.git"
  "--follow"
  "--type=file"
  "--type=symlink"
)
export FZF_CTRL_T_OPTS=$(echo "${FZF_CTRL_T_OPTS_ARRAY}")
export FZF_CTRL_T_COMMAND=$(echo "${FZF_CTRL_T_COMMAND_ARRAY}")
```

I'd like to draw your attention to these lines specifically:

```bash
FZF_CTRL_T_KEYBINDINGS_ARRAY=(
  "alt-b:become(bat {})"
  "alt-l:become(${${BAT_PAGER}:-less} {})"
  "alt-n:become(${EDITOR:-vim} {})"
)
FZF_CTRL_T_KEYBINDINGS=$(echo "${FZF_CTRL_T_KEYBINDINGS_ARRAY}" | sed 's/) a/),a/g')
```

Their ultimate purpose is to populate a string of keybindings that pipe the selected file into the appropriate program (e.g., `bat`, `less`). This string then get passed to `--bind` when setting `FZF_CTRL_T_OPTS`.

After sourcing everything, `FZF_CTRL_T_OPTS` looks like this:

```bash
❯ echo "${FZF_CTRL_T_OPTS}"
--bind='alt-b:become(bat {}),alt-l:become(less --chop-long-lines --header=1 --jump-target=3 --line-num-width=0 --LONG-PROMPT --no-number-headers --shift=4 --status-column --use-color --color=HGk --color=NGk {}),alt-n:become(nvim {})' --header-first --no-height --preview='bat --color=always --line-range=:500 {}' --preview-window=hidden
```

Seems fine, right? In fact, when I copy that string and pass it into `fzf` directly (i.e., `fzf --bind= [...] --preview-window=hidden`), my `alt-{b,l,n}` keybindings all work as intended. Here's an illustration using `alt-l` (`less`) and `alt-b` (`bat)`:

![Untitled](https://github.com/participant2/fzf/assets/62400541/3d1b0ba6-13b1-4c25-88de-aa813126bbfe)

**But here's where things get weird:** When I activate `fzf` via the `CTRL-T` keybinding and attempt `alt-{b,l,n}`, something completely different happens. Rather than opening the file with the desired program, it just `cat`s the file to stdout with all these escaped characters. Here's an example where I show this, first with `alt-b` then with `alt-l`:

![Untitled](https://github.com/participant2/fzf/assets/62400541/c12feb40-0e38-484e-8dbd-2c828788cc09)

In the end, this strange behavior prevents me from using my `alt-{b,l,n}` keybindings despite that they seem free of syntax errors.

Can you speculate what the issue might be? Note that I set all my `fzf` keybindings in the same way shown in my snippet, and everything has worked out until now.

Many thanks in advance for your ongoing discussions and support!

> In the end, the following keybinding works for me and now she's purring like a kitten!
> 
> ```shell
>   --bind=$'change:execute-silent:(
>     PREVIEW_SIZE=$(
>       curl -qsH "x-api-key: $FZF_API_KEY" localhost:$FZF_PORT \|
>         jq -r --argjson LINES $LINES \'[([($LINES/3), ($LINES - .matchCount - 5) ] | max),($LINES - 5)] | min | floor\'
>     );
>     curl -qsH "x-api-key: $FZF_API_KEY" localhost:$FZF_PORT -d "change-preview-window:$PREVIEW_SIZE"
>   ) &'
> ```
> 
> Thanks again for all your help!


Before setting `PREVIEW_SIZE=`, one can consider adding a check to ensure `progress` has reached 100.

```bash
--bind=$'change:execute-silent:(while (($(curl -s localhost:$FZF_PORT | jq -r \'.progress\') < 100));do; ! command kill -0 "$PPID" 2>/dev/null && break || sleep 0.1;done || exit ; PREVIEW_SIZE=…
```

---


> individual attention of a board-certified shell+`fzf` wizard like you

I'll do my best to assist you, but for more complex issues, you might want to reach out to experts like `participant2`.

---

> When I activate fzf via the CTRL-T keybinding and attempt alt-{b,l,n}, something completely different happens. Rather than opening the file with the desired program, it just cats the file to stdout with all these escaped characters.

I assume your <kbd>⌃ Control</kbd> + <kbd>T</kbd> hotkey is assigned to the unmodified `fzf-file-widget`?

```bash
bindkey | grep fzf-file-widget
# "^T" fzf-file-widget
```

Your response is then passed through the `__fsel` and assigned to the `LBUFFER`, which significantly
alters the output. This occurs because the widget is attempting to place the command on the command
line while escaping special characters. See related discussion[^1].


https://github.com/participant2/fzf/blob/952b6af4454ed55626d78e3845c6b5b640ac831d/shell/key-bindings.zsh#L63-L68

https://github.com/participant2/fzf/blob/952b6af4454ed55626d78e3845c6b5b640ac831d/shell/key-bindings.zsh#L42-L56

### Possible options:
1. You would need to create your own widget or modify the existing one. 
2. Instead of using `"alt-b:become(bat {})"`, consider using `"alt-b:execute(bat {} >/dev/tty)"` [^2]

---

>[!NOTE]
> This line appears to be a _hacky_ workaround:
> ```bash
> FZF_CTRL_T_KEYBINDINGS=$(echo "${FZF_CTRL_T_KEYBINDINGS_ARRAY}" | sed 's/) a/),a/g')
> ```
> The following format may be a better alternative in `zsh` [^3]
> ```bash
> FZF_CTRL_T_KEYBINDINGS="${(j:,:)FZF_CTRL_T_KEYBINDINGS_ARRAY}"
> ```

[^1]: [Manual output on enter, no linebreak. · Discussion #3514](https://github.com/participant2/fzf/discussions/3514)
[^2]: [Issue #2579](https://github.com/participant2/fzf/issues/2579#issuecomment-919770417)
[^3]: [zsh: 14 Parameter-Expansion-Flags](https://<redacted-host>/Doc/Release/Expansion.html#Parameter-Expansion-Flags)

comments.body:
> Hi [@participant1](https://github.com/participant1) , seems this command is not working in `fzf v0.68.0`:

Right, in Bash it wont work for me either; it should work with `--with-shell 'zsh -dfc'`

**BUT**, since this demo was created, the maintainer has introduced new
`FZF_*` environment variables that make this _"hack"_ outdated.

Could you take a look at the `0.46.0` CHANGELOG[^1]? The maintainer provided a
**transformer** example that may work out of the box for you, or with slight
adjustments if needed, maybe u would use different values or other trigger
events (`focus`, `change`, ...).

```bash
# Script to dynamically resize the preview window by 'participant2'
transformer='
# 1 line for info, another for the prompt, and 2 more lines for the preview window border
lines=$(( FZF_LINES - FZF_MATCH_COUNT - 4 ))
if [[ $FZF_MATCH_COUNT -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "change-preview-window:hidden"
elif [[ $lines -gt 3 ]]; then
  echo "change-preview-window:$lines"
elif [[ $FZF_PREVIEW_LINES -ne 3 ]]; then
  echo "change-preview-window:3"
fi'

find . -type f -maxdepth 1 | FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS="" fzf \
  --preview 'bat --color=always {}' \
  --preview-window 'up,border-bottom' \
  --bind "result:transform:$transformer" \
  --bind "resize:transform:$transformer"
```


[^1]: https://github.com/participant2/fzf/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#0460
